hints.title: Priority of Extending Existing Sequences
hints.text: When placing an element x, it is always preferable to append it to an already existing valid chain ending at x - 1 rather than starting a new one.

hints.title: Forming Fresh Triplet Chains
hints.text: If x cannot extend an existing sequence, it must be capable of starting a new valid sequence of at least three elements using x + 1 and x + 2.

hints.title: Tracking Element Frequencies and Vacancies
hints.text: Track remaining counts and chain terminations. If x - 1 has an active termination, decrement it and record a termination at x; otherwise check if x + 1 and x + 2 exist; if neither holds, partition is impossible.

hints.title: See the blueprint

variables: N: number of elements in nums
complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving linear O(N) time and linear O(N) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Backtracking over all possible groupings leads to exponential time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Counting frequencies and tail ends guarantees greedy decision validity in linear time.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should understand why extending an existing sequence never hurts future triplets.
